title: Nutritional Status as a Predictor of Treatment Outcomes in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease—A Prospective Cohort Study
summary: Patients with peripheral arterial disease often experience additional nutritional problems or malnutrition. This study aims to investigate whether nutritional status influences the further course of the disease. To this end, established nutritional questionnaires, laboratory test results, and clinical data will be analyzed. The aim is to determine whether patients at increased nutritional risk are more likely to develop complications or have poorer treatment outcomes.

interventions.name: Patients with confirmed peripheral arterial disease (Fontaine stages II–IV) who present at the University Hospital of Augsburg as outpatients or inpatients are enrolled in the study after receiving informed consent. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD), Fontaine Stages II–IV
Exclusion criteria:
Acute systemic inflammatory diseases
Malignant disease with a limited life expectancy (< 6 months)
Inability to perform a nutritional screening (e.g., lack of consent, noncompliance, inability to communicate, language barrier, legal guardianship)
Major amputations
